title: By the River
focus: despair and renewal by the river

teacherSummary.text: Siddhartha reaches the river sick of himself and comes close to ending his life (By the River, paras. 2–5; referenced, not quoted). From deep within comes the sacred word Om, and he falls into a deep sleep under a coconut tree. He wakes renewed; Govinda, now a monk, has watched over him without recognizing him. Siddhartha reflects that he had to experience despair to learn its emptiness, and decides to stay by the river.

I read “Now, Siddhartha smiled” slowly and put it in my own words: Govinda, now a monk, has watched over a sleeping stranger and does not recognize him; when he asks how the stranger knows his name, Siddhartha smiles. Next, craft. I notice the line is only four words, set alone after the monk's puzzled question, so the smile answers him before any words do. Why does Siddhartha smile when the monk asks how he knows his name?
